visual_text: Parkinson's doses: their times, not the ward's
Can doses be given at their own times?
Can they keep taking their own supply?
If they can't swallow or are told not to eat, what is the plan?
Standard used in one English hospital audit: within 30 minutes of the person's own time
Dublin hospital study: 52 in 100 doses more than 30 minutes late
Richard et al., Mov Disord Clin Pract 2022; Omer et al., Cureus 2025
alt_text: Drawn hospital bay: an older man sits in a chair with his own pill organiser and walking frame in front of him, while his daughter holding a folder and a nurse stand by. Three questions: can doses be given at their own times, can they keep their own supply, and what is the plan if they can't swallow. A Dublin study found 52 in 100 doses over 30 minutes late.
design_instructions: Single card, sand ground. Kit hospital bay: older man seated with pill organiser and standard walking frame, daughter with folder, nurse; question ticks below and audit panel. Wall clock and trolley omitted.
